Het platform wordt beheerd door LVNL, ondersteund door een externe specialistische ServiceNow-partner. LVNL wenst een duurzame samenwerking aan te gaan met één leverancier die het beheer, de ondersteuning en de doorontwikkeling van het platform kan verzorgen. De gewenste dienstverlening bestaat in hoofdlijn uit twee diensten, te weten Managed Services (Beheer) en Consultancy. De overeenkomst treedt naar verwachting in werking medio februari 2027. description: Helen Sähköverkko Oy is building new 400 kV substation in Sörnäinen, Helsinki Finland. Delivery of 63 MVAr 21 kV Variable Shunt Reactor (VSR) Synthetic Ester Oil-Immersed including: - Manufacturing of reactor with fittings and accessories - Testing - All necessary logistics e.g. - Sea transportation to Finland - Loading and unloading on the railway cart - Loading and unloading on road truck and transport to the site - Supplier may choose the means and route of transportation - All organizational work needed for logistics: arrangement of transportation from factory to site, customs clearance and forwarding - Unloading on the foundation - Erection, testing and commissioning at site.

title: COOP Wharf Elevation Works at L'Étang-du-Nord Fishing Harbour, Magdalen Islands, Quebec
description: The elevation works for the COOP Wharf at L’Étang-du-Nord Fishing Harbour in the Magdalen Islands include, but are not limited to, the following work: • Partial demolition of existing wharves and reuse of recovered stone. • Installation of a containment curtain and a floating boom to retain driftwood and suspended particles during wharf demolition or dredging activities required for preparation of the granular foundation. • Excavation of the seabed (contaminated sediments) to allow for the installation of the granular foundation for the new crib structures. • Work required for the installation of the granular foundation of the new timber crib wharves. • Supply of all materials required for the construction of ACC-treated timber crib wharves. • Demolition of the riprap protection on one side of the wharf approach. • Placement of pit run and granular materials for the widening of the wharf approach. • Stockpiling (according to potential contamination) and characterization of dredged materials to construct the granular base for the new crib structures. • Disposal and/or beneficial use of dredged sediments at authorized sites. • Civil works for the installation of electrical and potable water services to the new wharf. • Paving works for the wharf approach. • Supply and installation of electrical distribution, lighting and water system components.

title: Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) for Enniskillen Road Upgrade
description: DEFENCE CONSTRUCTION CANADA (DCC) – Project No. HQ04022_88127 – Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) for Enniskillen Road Upgrade, Gagetown, NB DEFENCE CONSTRUCTION CANADA (DCC) – Project No. HQ04022_88127 – Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) for Enniskillen Road Upgrade, Gagetown, NB Defence Construction Canada (DCC) invites general contractors to express their interest in providing all labour, materials, and equipment necessary for the Enniskillen Road Upgrade at Gagetown, NB This Request for Expression of Interest (RFEOI) is the first step of a two-step solicitation process, the second step being the Tender Phase.  Only general contractors that have expressed their interest through the Electronic Bidding System prior to the closing date and time of this RFEOI will be invited to submit a proposal at the second stage. Only submissions received in accordance with the requirements of the Electronic Bidding System will be considered. Only the general contractors who will have responded to this RFEOI will be invited to submit a bid during the Tender Phase. DCC reserves the right to terminate this solicitation at the end of the RFEOI. As part of Canada’s commitment to maximize the participation of Indigenous Businesses, bidders are advised that this solicitation includes an Indigenous Benefits Plan (IBP). The Contractor will have to include Indigenous businesses (or eligible joint ventures) as subcontractors or suppliers to this project. Further details will be provided in the Tender phase. This solicitation is being conducted in accordance with the requirements set out in the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA). Project background A detailed project background can be reviewed in the Building Summary Documents Technical plans and specifications are not available during this RFEOI and will be provided during the Tender Phase; however, the Standard Construction Contract Documents for Electronic Bidding, DCL 250E, are available on DCC's website: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. Tenderers are advised that this contract is subject to DCC's Procurement Code of Conduct, which can be downloaded at https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/forms. A contractor or supplier who has been declared ineligible or suspended by Public Services and Procurement Canada under its Ineligibility and Suspension Policy and whose period of ineligibility or suspension may not have expired will not be able to proceed to the second stage. Bid security will be required during the Tender Phase in accordance with DCL193E- Instructions for Bidders for Electronic Bidding item 5. Estimate The Rough Order Magnitude estimate / Construction Cost Limit for this Contract is $ 25,642,471.00. This amount includes all construction costs, on-site work (including all required services, parking, and landscaping), site utilities, necessary redundant mechanical systems, communication conduits and wiring, backup power equipment, built-in equipment, built-in furniture, and inflation to achieve substantial completion. This amount excludes HST, design costs, travel and disbursements, consultant fees and expenses, movable equipment and furniture, IT equipment and contingencies. Schedule DCC will proceed with the Tender Phase around November - December 2026. The works shall reach substantial completion no later than October 15, 2027 and shall be completed no later than November 15, 2027.\ Site visit No site visits will be offered during the RFEOI however, during the Tender Phase, bidders will be invited to a site visit. Access to information Act Tenderers are advised that DCC is subject to the provisions of the Access to Information Act (Canada). Information submitted may be eligible for disclosure in accordance with the requirements of the Act. Questions and clarifications Any questions or requests for clarification must be submitted in writing to DCC's Coordinator, Contract Services whose contact information can be found in the Electronic Bid System. DCC reserves the right to request clarification and/or confirmation regarding any aspect of this RFEOI to the Tenderer. In such a case, the Coordinator, Contract Services will be responsible for making the request. The request for clarification and/or confirmation will be sent to the contact person identified on the Electronic Submission System. Language of the Tender and the contract By submitting a response to this RFEOI, Tenderers will be invited to choose the desired official language for the tender documents and any resulting contract. In the Tender Phase, tender documents will be published in the language chosen by the Tenderer in the Electronic Bid System. Unless otherwise specified in the Contract, all Contract Documents to which the Contract applies or refers, as well as all deliverables, documents, reports and results of the work, services or goods that the Contractor submits, provides, or delivers to DCC or Canada in connection with the performance of the Contract, shall be in the language chosen by the Contractor on the Electronic Bid System. Joint venture A joint venture is an association of two or more parties that pools their funds, assets, knowledge, expertise, or other resources into a joint business venture, sometimes called a consortium, to bid together for a requirement. Tenderers submitting interest as a joint venture will be required to clearly indicate in the Electronic Submission System that they are forming a joint venture and should provide the following information: the name of the joint venture, if applicable, the name of the representative of the joint venture, i.e., the member chosen by the other members to represent them, if applicable, the name of each member of the joint venture. Closing location Responses to this RFEOI must be received through the Electronic Bidding System.  Responses sent by fax, mail or email will not be accepted.  Closing Date and Time The closing date and time indicated in the Electronic Submission System will be the official closing date and time of this RFEOI.      Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

title: Belgium – Time accounting or human resources software development services – Aankoop, implementatie en onderhoud van een Applicant Tracking System (ATS)
description: Deze opdracht betreft de aankoop, implementatie en onderhoud van een Applicant Tracking System (ATS), waarbij de opdrachtnemer in staat voor het rekruteren van nieuwe medewerkers . De doelstelling is om het volledige wervings- en selectieproces te beheren binnen één tool, in een cloudtoepassing, waar noodzakelijk of nuttig via integratie met andere interne en externe platformen om zo een maximaal efficiënte en geautomatiseerde werking te garanderen. Stad Brugge, OCMW Brugge en de verenigingen van het OCMW Brugge werken vanuit een wetgevend kader (rechtspositieregeling), wat betekent dat er een aantal extra noden bestaan ten opzichte van een bedrijf van soortgelijke grootte uit de private sector. Die verschillen zijn niet zozeer inhoudelijk van aard, maar eerder juridisch en procedureel. Het systeem moet een juridisch robuust, transparant en objectief proces ondersteunen dat voldoet aan de principes van gelijkheid, non-discriminatie, motiveringsplicht en openbaarheid, met vaste procedures, uniforme selectiecriteria en de nodige rapporteringsmogelijkheden. Tegelijk moet het ATS voldoende flexibiliteit en gebruiksvriendelijkheid bieden voor zowel de backend gebruiker als de sollicitant om doorlooptijden te beheersen, kandidaat- en gebruikerservaring te verbeteren en een modern selectieproces toe te laten.

description: This is a solicitation for non-commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR)/Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 13 as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Naval Surface Warfare Center Indian Head Division (NSWC IHD), located in Indian Head, Maryland, intends to award a firm-fixed-price (FFP) purchase order using Simplified Acquisition Procedures for MIL-Spec Wood Crates IAW ASTM D6880/PPP-B-621. Quotes are being requested for the manufacture of MIL-Spec wood shipping crates roughly 81 x 8 x 8 inches. title: Inspect and Repair of 13.2KV Main Switchgear
description: The U.S. Coast Guard Academy requires a qualified, licensed electrical contractor to inspect, repair as necessary, test, and restore Eaton/Cutler-Hammer MVS2 13.2 kV medium-voltage load interrupter switchgear, with primary work focused on Cabinet 5 and the associated 15 kV feeder cable serving Smith Hall. The contractor shall inspect Cabinet 5 for damage or missing/cannibalized components; remove and replace three Eaton 15CLE-250E fuses; procure and deliver three additional matching fuses for on-site spares; perform insulation-resistance testing of the feeder cable in accordance with current ANSI/NETA standards; provide certified test and field-service reports; coordinate all required outages and lockout/tagout procedures with the Government; and safely re-energize the cabinet and feeder upon successful completion of repairs and testing. All work shall comply with applicable OSHA, NFPA 70E, federal, state, and local requirements, including proper licensed personnel, arc-flash personal protective equipment, site protection, cleanup, and disposal of waste materials.

title: LETTER OF INTEREST (LOI) – DETERMINATION OF V50 VELOCITIES FOR SELECTED PROJECTILES
description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) Specialized Firearms Support Services (SFSS) supports firearms classification activities, including determining whether certain devices meet the definition of a firearm under section 2 of the Criminal Code. A recurring challenge in the technical assessment of low-velocity projectile devices is determining whether a device is capable of causing serious bodily injury and therefore meeting the Criminal Code definition of a firearm. These assessments require scientifically defensible data regarding the performance and injury potential of projectiles fired from such devices. To support these assessments, SFSS is exploring a means of experimentally determine V50 ballistic limit velocities for a variety of projectiles commonly used in airguns, airsoft devices, and similar low-velocity projectile devices. The resulting information may support firearms classification activities and contribute to our broader technical understanding of projectile performance and injury potential. Canada is particularly interested in research that expands upon the methodology and findings presented in AD3, AD4, and AD5. Unlike the referenced studies, which focused on a limited number of airguns and projectile types, the potential requirement may involve testing a broader range of projectiles and devices commonly encountered in firearms-classification activities, including airguns, airsoft devices, and other low-velocity projectile devices.

title: PCB Transformer Replacements at Beaver Creek Institution -Minimum
description: The Correctional Service Canada (CSC) requires the removal and replacement of two transformers at Beaver Creek Institution (Minimum) prior to December 31, 2026 to comply with federal regulations established under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act and the polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) Regulations. One existing pad-mounted transformer, installed in 1975, contains polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) at a concentration of 172 ppm, which exceeds the regulatory threshold. A second pole-mounted transformer has reached the end of its service life and, due to its age, may contain PCBs. Both transformers must be removed and replaced prior to the regulatory deadline of December 31, 2026. The work includes the supply and installation of replacement transformers, disposal of PCB-contaminated equipment and associated oil in accordance with applicable regulations, coordination of electrical outages and commissioning activities, and restoration of affected areas.

title: iPSC Culture and Differentiation
description: NOTICE OF INTENT � SOLE-SOURCE ACQUISITION Notice No.: The National Institutes of Health (NIH), National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS), intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to Creative Biolab Inc. for culture all cells and differentiate them, expand their cell populations to more than 20 million, collect them, verify cell count, and send them back to us. Description of the Requirement The primary objective of this study is to sequence and analyze the 4q35 locus on Chromosome 4 for several years. This locus is a gene-poor and extremely long (>100K) region of DNA that consists of many repetitive sequences which makes sequencing and analysis extremely difficult. To sequence this locus using Nanopore Sequencing technology. To expand the number of samples for our experiment, we looked for a company that can handle numerous cell lines and follow the protocol that we provide. Creative Biolabs is the only company/research institute that has been able to perform differentiation within 3 months and has the ability to follow our protocol with numerous cell lines. Justification for the Proposed Sole-Source Acquisition The Government intends to solicit from a single source pursuant to FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Only Creative Biolabs was willing to follow our exact protocol and had the logistical capacity to handle the large number of cell lines that we need to analyze, which is vital to research at the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences. Response Information This notice is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required preventive maintenance and remedial repair services for the specified instrument and meet all applicable technical and operational requirements. The Government will review timely submissions to determine whether another responsible source is capable of satisfying the requirement and whether a competitive acquisition is appropriate. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source can satisfy the requirement. Capability statements must be submitted electronically to verne.griffin@nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on November 13, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98027Q00053 in the subject line of the submission.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source: Fuel Storage Services at West Oahu, HI
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE: This notice is being published in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subpart 5.101 requiring dissemination of information for proposed contract actions. This is a notice of intent to make a single source award contract and is not a request for competitive proposals. The statutory authority for the use of other than full and open competition procedure for this procurement is prescribed by FAR 6.103-1, only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy the agency�s requirements. DLA Energy intends to issue a four-year base, with one, five-year option period and six one-month options firm fixed price single source award contract to IES Downstream, LLC (IES), in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1), Only One Responsible Source. The contract will provide services with the capability to receive via Tanker/Barge and Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam (JBPHH)/Red Hill (RH) tank farm and commercial/refinery pipeline, store, protect, and ship Aviation Turbine Fuel Grades Jet-A, JP-5 and Naval Distillate Fuel Grade F-76 via Tanker/Barge, JBPHH pipeline, and tank truck with a storage fill capacity of 2,051,000 barrels (BBLS). Background: IES provides contract services for the receipt and distribution of aviation fuel at West Oahu, Hawaii. Currently, the company receives Government-owned Aviation Turbine Fuel Grades Jet-A and JP-5) and Naval Distillate Fuel Grade F-76 via tanker/barge and contractor furnished pipeline system. This arrangement involves the unloading of fuel and its subsequent handling within IES's facilities. The Government intends to award a follow-on contract for these services at West Oahu, Hawaii, scheduled for Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27). This upcoming contract specifies an annual throughput requirement of 3,500,000 barrels of Aviation Turbine Fuel and Naval Distillate Fuel. To fulfill the requirement would require the construction of a pipeline and subsequent connection point to the Government�s pipeline by the start of the performance period (October 26, 2027). Competitive Environment: There are no planned actions to address barriers that would create a more competitive procurement environment for dock services at West Oahu, Hawaii. Objectives: The objective of the contract is to ensure uninterrupted support for the government customers' Jet and Naval Distillate fuel needs.

title: Lock, Key, and TRAKA Key Management Systems Maintenance and Support Services
description: RFQ Amendment 1: The purposes of Amendment 1 are to: Provide the Government's response to a question received from a prospective contractor regarding the Secret Facility Clearance (FCL) and TRAKA-authorized reseller/installer requirements. Issue a revised solicitation and Statement of Work (SOW) to clarify the requirements for the prime contractor and subcontractors regarding the final Secret FCL and TRAKA authorization. Change the quotation due date from Monday, November 9, 2026 by 12:00 pm EST to no later than 9:00 am EST on Thursday, November 12, 2026. Contractor Question and Government Response: Question: Can the active final Secret Facility Clearance (FCL) and TRAKA-authorized reseller/installer requirements be satisfied through an eligible subcontractor or teaming partner, or must the prime offeror itself possess both requirements at the time of award? Government Response: The prime contractor must independently possess an active, final Secret Facility Clearance (FCL) at the time of award and maintain the required clearance throughout contract performance. This requirement cannot be satisfied through a subcontractor or teaming partner, regardless of subcontracting arrangements. However, the TRAKA-authorized reseller and installer requirements may be satisfied through an eligible subcontractor. The prime contractor is not required to independently possess TRAKA authorization, provided the proposed subcontractor holds the required authorization and will perform the applicable TRAKA-related services. Offerors must provide documentation demonstrating the required TRAKA authorization held by either the prime contractor or its proposed subcontractor. The prime contractor remains responsible for ensuring compliance with all contract requirements, including applicable personnel security, facility access, and subcontractor approval requirements. Revised Solicitation and Statement of Work The solicitation and SOW are revised to reflect the following requirements: 1. Secret Facility Clearance (FCL) The prime contractor must possess an active, final Secret FCL at the time of award and maintain the required clearance throughout contract performance. A subcontractor's or teaming partner's FCL cannot be used to satisfy this requirement. Interim facility clearances are not acceptable. 2. TRAKA-Authorized Reseller and Installer The TRAKA-authorized reseller and installer requirements may be satisfied by either the prime contractor or an eligible subcontractor. If relying on a subcontractor, the offeror must identify the proposed subcontractor and provide documentation demonstrating its current TRAKA-authorized reseller and installer status. 3. Technical Evaluation The Government will evaluate compliance with the final Secret FCL requirement and TRAKA authorization requirement in accordance with the revised solicitation and SOW. Failure to meet either mandatory requirement will result in a determination of technical unacceptability. Attachments Revised Solicitation: RFQ 2099CF27Q00010, Amendment 0001 Revised Statement of Work (SOW): Lock, Key, and TRAKA Key Management System Maintenance and Support Services All other terms and conditions of the solicitation remain unchanged unless otherwise specified in this amendment. See attachment RFQ 2099CF27Q00010 Amendment 1 for complete details. __________________________________________________________________ Original RFQ: The Treasury Common Services Center (TCSC), on behalf of the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), is soliciting quotations for Lock, Key, and TRAKA Key Management System Maintenance and Support Services. This acquisition is a 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside under NAICS Code 561621 � Security Systems Services, with a corresponding small business size standard of $25 million in average annual receipts. Only responsible small business concerns that qualify as small under the applicable NAICS code and meet all solicitation requirements are eligible for award. The contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, management, materials, equipment, software licenses, technical support, and incidental services necessary to maintain FinCEN�s physical security and key-control systems. Services will be performed on an as-needed basis and may include preventive and corrective maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, replacement, installation, relocation, testing, configuration, software support, and emergency services. The systems and equipment covered by this requirement include TRAKA electronic key-management cabinets and associated software, Medeco high-security lock cores and related hardware, Kaba Mas X10 high-security locks, other high-security and manual door-locking hardware, and associated components, cabling, licenses, and ancillary equipment. The Government anticipates awarding a time-and-materials contract with an anticipated period of performance of five years, base period and four (4) option periods. The not-to-exceed (NTE) ceiling is $40,000 for each one-year contract period. If all four option periods are exercised, the maximum potential contract ceiling is $200,000. The Contractor must be a TRAKA-authorized reseller and installer and must possess an active, final Secret Facility Clearance (FCL) at the time of award. Offerors shall provide documentation demonstrating current TRAKA authorization and the capability to maintain, repair, install, and support FinCEN�s existing TRAKA, Medeco, Kaba Mas, Lockmasters, and associated locking systems, including applicable proprietary equipment, software, licensing, integration, and compatibility requirements. Contractor personnel performing services under the resulting contract must possess final Secret personnel security clearances before beginning performance and satisfy all applicable personnel-security, continuous vetting, and facility-access requirements identified in Section 7.0 of the Statement of Work. Interim facility and personnel security clearances will not be accepted. The Government will verify the required facility clearance prior to award and personnel clearance and access requirements prior to performance. Performance will occur at FinCEN facilities located in Washington, DC, and Vienna, Virginia.
